Treatment summary
The patient presented following a rear-end mootr vehcile collision with complaints of
right knee pain and reduced range of motion. The reported mechanism of injury is
consistent with the knee injury described, and the presentation is plausible for a
collision of this type. Over the course of 19 visits, care included physical
examination, imaging review, a structured rehabilitation program, and activity
modification. The treatment course followed a typical progression, with visit
frequency decreasing and symptoms easing as the patient improved. Some examination
findings, including joint line tenderness and reduced flexion, support the reported
injury, while other orthopedic tests and neurovascular checks were within normal
limits. No prior injury to the same knee is known from the patient history. Billing
records show two similar charges on the same date of service, which are currently under
review for accuracy and duplication. Ongoing monitoring and a home exercise plan were
recommended at discharge from active care.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
